full_judgment:
3. The defendant petitioner contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations contending that the suit was not maintainable and the same was barred by limitation. The story of oral agreement for sale is absolutely false and he did not receive Taka 30,000 as earnest money. The defendant No. 1 is a landless cultivator. The original owner of the suit land is Government and the Government leased out the same to him for a period of 15 years. Accordingly a deed of lease was executed on 28-11-1978. In 1988, this defendant petitioner gave shelter to the plaintiffs in the suit land considering the humanitarian approach and who gave assurance to this petitioner that they would vacate the possession of the suit land. Thereafter, the petitioner requested the plaintiffs repeatedly to vacate possession but they did not pay any heed. Few days thereafter miscreants killed a son of defendant and he was mentally disturbed so he could not compel the plaintiffs to vacate the suit land. A salish was held in Poush, 1399 BS and in that salish the plaintiffs assured the petitioner that they would leave possession. In the meantime, the petitioner decided to sell 0.50 acre of land to Bhojeshwar Girl High School and receiving Taka 15,000 he delivered possession of that land to the said school. In such view of the matter the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 8. Mr. Khan submits that as the petitioner having had no saleable interest in the suit land at the time of oral agreement so the said agreement is invalid agreement in the eye of law. It is true that at the time of making agreement the defendant petitioner had no saleable interest in the suit land but it appears from the Ext Ka, the kabuliyat, as produced by the defendant-petitioner, that there was a condition that after expiry of 15 years the title of the suit land should be vested with the petitioner free from all encumbrances. As per provision of section 81 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the Government may lease out any land for any particular period and the rights and liabilities of such a lease shall be governed by such terms and conditions as may be set forth in the lease. It appears from the terms of lease that after expiry of 15 years the instant lease should be treated as permanent lease. So, after expiry of said period the petitioner's title in the suit land has become absolute. The lease deed was executed on 28-11-1978 and 15 years expired on 28-11-1993, that is, after 28-11-1993 the defendant petitioner acquired absolute ownership in the land under dispute. Where a person having partial interest in certain property, transfers a larger interest and subsequently acquired that interest, in that case the provision of section 43 of the Transfer of Property Act applies and the transferee is entitled to get interest so acquired. The rule in section 43 of the Transfer of Property Act applies in the case of lease also. Where a lessee had an infirm title and subsequently acquired title he could be compelled to carry out the contract. In such view of the matter, I am of the opinion that as the title of the petitioner became absolute after expiry of 15 years from the date of lease so he is bound by contract for sale. 

 9. Mr. Khan, lastly, submits that the instant suit was barred by limitation. It appears in the plaint that the plaintiff stated that in the middle of December 1994, the petitioner denied to execute and register the sale deed and the instant suit was filed on 26-1-1995. The limitation of the instant suit will run from the date of such refusal. The learned Courts below considered the evidence and found the story of refusal to execute and register the sale deed true. Both the Courts below observed that the plaintiffs have been able to prove their cause of aection and held that the instant suit was not barred by limitation. I do not find any illegality in the observation made by the learned Courts below about the limitation.
